title: Dispatch OGF 2: People in the Pears Demand Their Privacy
summary: A grower faces questions about scenes taken from rooms she has never entered.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Institute has confirmed seven scenes inside fruit from Rill Orchard against accounts from the people depicted. Four show events known only to their participants. One shows an empty room shortly after a family left it; another shows two people meeting in a place neither has named publicly.

Mrs. Rill says she planted her oldest trees from local stock. Five years ago, her late son Peter grafted three branches with a cutting purchased from a travelling Eidetician. He called it mirrorwood. Mrs. Rill kept the grafts because they were the last work he did in the orchard before his death.

Alderman Felix Dorne has asked the Institute to hold the unsold harvest. He says a vendor should not be permitted to trade in another person’s private life, regardless of how the images were made. Dr. Saye agrees that the fruit should be kept out of circulation but has asked that none be destroyed before its origin is understood.

Yesterday Mrs. Rill brought one pear to the Institute herself. It shows Peter at the orchard gate, carrying a spade and looking back toward the house. She had not seen him leave on that morning. She says he died three weeks later and asks to keep this one fruit when the examination is over.

“I thought they showed things we remembered,” she told our reporter. “Then I saw him do something I never knew he had done. Perhaps the trees remember for themselves.” Dr. Saye has begun comparing each image with the position of the branch on which its fruit grew.
